title: Clinical AI Interpretation: Limits and Escalation
summary: Learn how an AI medical interpreter works in real clinical care, where AI medical interpretation can break down, and when to pause, clarify.
body_markdown:
###


Common limitations include unclear audio, long speaking turns, overlapping speakers, dialect mismatch, unfamiliar terminology, code-switching, number errors, negation errors, and difficulty when the source speech is incomplete or ambiguous.


###


Stop before adding more information, repeat the source statement in a shorter form, isolate numbers or medication names, and confirm the corrected meaning with the patient.


###


Consider another method when repeated clarification does not resolve the communication problem, the patient requests another option, an accessibility need calls for a different pathway, or hospital policy specifies another method.


###


No single encounter label determines the right method in every case. The care team should consider communication quality, patient preference, accessibility needs, local policy, and whether the current method is working.


###


Yes, when the system is performing well and the patient and clinician can communicate clearly. Teams should still know how to pause, clarify, and change methods if the communication breaks down.
